In RESTful API conventions, which HTTP verb and status code represent a successful update that modifies an existing resource completely?

options.value: PUT with HTTP 200 OK (or 204 No Content)
DELETE with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed

explanation.value: PUT is idempotent and replaces an existing target resource with the requested payload, returning 200 OK or 204 No Content.

prompt.value: In Flask / Jinja2 web applications, what mechanism prevents Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on form submissions?

options.value: Embedding a cryptographically signed, session-tied CSRF token in the form verified server-side
Storing all passwords in client-side localStorage
Allowing wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` headers on POST endpoints
Encrypting the database connection string with MD5

explanation.value: CSRF tokens ensure that state-changing requests originate from an authentic user session inside the web application.

prompt.value: In SQLite / SQLAlchemy, what command or constraint ensures that deleting a parent record automatically removes all associated child records?

options.value: `ON DELETE CASCADE` on the foreign key constraint
`ON DELETE SET NULL` on the primary key
`UNIQUE INDEX` on the parent primary key

explanation.value: CASCADE triggers automatic deletion of dependent foreign key rows when the referenced parent row is deleted.

prompt.value: In client-server web architecture, what is the key difference between Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and Single Page Applications (SPA)?

options.value: In SSR, full HTML is rendered on the server per request; in SPAs, the browser dynamically updates the DOM using JSON from an API
In SSR, no database is required; in SPAs, all data must reside in browser cookies
SSR cannot use CSS; SPAs cannot use JavaScript
SPAs execute SQL queries directly from client-side JavaScript

explanation.value: SSR builds complete HTML on the backend, while SPAs load a static shell and fetch data via REST APIs.
